learningModules.title: Module 1: Onboarding Drop-off Anatomy
learningModules.description: Understand the precise activation failure at step 3 and why it produces a 92% 30-day churn rate for users who skip it.
learningModules.content:
Your onboarding has 4 steps. Steps 1 and 2 complete at 61% — reasonable for a SaaS product. Step 3 (analytics integration) drops to 18%. Of the 82% who skip or abandon step 3, 92% churn within 30 days.

The root mechanism is a context-switch cascade: step 3 requires users to leave your product, navigate to a third-party platform, locate credentials they may not know the location of, copy them, return, paste correctly, and wait for validation. This is 6 sequential actions with a mean completion time of 4.2 minutes — all before the user has seen a single data point from your product.

The critical insight: users do not abandon because the integration is hard. They abandon because they have not yet experienced the aha-moment that would justify the effort. Value must precede friction, not follow it.

Benchmark: SaaS products that defer integration gates to post-aha-moment see 3.4x higher 30-day retention versus products that require integration at step 1–3.

learningModules.title: Module 2: Demo Data Bypass — The Aha-Moment First Fix
learningModules.description: Implement a sample data bypass that lets users experience the core product value before requiring any integration effort.
learningModules.content:
The fix has two components: a bypass option and a re-engagement trigger.

Component 1 — Demo Data Bypass: Add a secondary CTA below the integration form. Label: 'Explore with benchmark data →'. This routes users into a fully functional dashboard seeded with anonymized benchmark data from your industry vertical. The data should be realistic and slightly better than average — aspirational but credible.

Design note: the bypass button must not look like an escape hatch. It should look like the smarter path. Use the same visual weight as the primary integration CTA. Never label it 'Skip' — frame it as acceleration, not avoidance.

Component 2 — Re-engagement trigger: On day 2 (after users have interacted with demo data 2+ times), trigger an in-app message: 'You've explored [X] reports in demo mode. Connect your real data to see your actual numbers — it takes 90 seconds.' Now the integration request arrives post-value, not pre-value.

Expected outcome: 30-day activation rate increase from 18% to 55–70% based on comparable implementations.

learningModules.title: Module 3: Activation Telemetry — 6 Events That Reveal Everything
learningModules.description: Instrument your onboarding sequence with PostHog events to measure activation health and identify micro-friction points in real time.
learningModules.content:
Deploy in this exact priority order:

1. posthog.capture('onboarding_step_complete', { step: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 }) — your funnel spine
2. posthog.capture('integration_attempted') — distinguishes intent from completion
3. posthog.capture('integration_completed') — the hard gate metric
4. posthog.capture('demo_data_activated') — measures bypass adoption
5. posthog.capture('first_insight_viewed') — the aha-moment indicator
6. posthog.capture('re_engagement_prompt_clicked') — measures day-2 trigger effectiveness

Build two PostHog funnels:
— Current path: step_1 → step_2 → integration_attempted → integration_completed → first_insight_viewed
— New path: step_1 → step_2 → demo_data_activated → first_insight_viewed → integration_completed

The second funnel should show a dramatically higher first_insight_viewed rate — this is your leading indicator that the fix is working before 30-day retention data is available.

learningModules.title: Module 4: Weekly Activation Review Ritual
learningModules.description: The 15-minute weekly process to monitor activation health and iterate systematically without losing signal in the noise.
learningModules.content:
Every Monday, 15 minutes, in this order:

1. Open your PostHog funnel dashboard. Check the step_1 → first_insight_viewed conversion rate. If it moved more than ±5 points from the prior week, investigate the cause before making any changes.

2. Review demo_data_activated / total_signups ratio. Target: >60% of users who reach step 3 choose the demo path. If below 40%, the bypass button is not prominent enough.

3. Check re_engagement_prompt_clicked rate (day-2 trigger). Target: >35% click-through. If below 20%, the message copy or timing needs adjustment.

4. Review integration_completed rate among users who initially took the demo path. This is your proxy for long-term integration quality — users who chose demo first should convert to real integration at >50% within 14 days.

Rule: change one variable per week maximum. Testing two changes simultaneously makes it impossible to attribute performance delta to a specific cause. Activation optimization is a controlled experiment, not a sprint.

checklist.task: Audit step 3 integration flow — count every required action and context switch
checklist.tip: The current count is 6 actions. Your target post-fix is 1 action (click 'Explore with benchmark data') or 3 actions max if integration proceeds directly.

checklist.task: Design and ship the 'Explore with benchmark data' bypass button at step 3
checklist.tip: Equal visual weight to the primary CTA. Label it as acceleration, not escape. Test 'See your benchmark performance →' as the copy.

checklist.task: Seed dashboard with realistic, aspirational benchmark data for your primary industry vertical
checklist.tip: Data should be 15–20% better than industry average — aspirational but not unbelievable. Users who see impressive demo data are more motivated to integrate their real data.
Start with onboarding_step_complete and first_insight_viewed — these two events give you 80% of the signal you need to diagnose activation problems.

checklist.task: Build PostHog activation funnel and schedule Monday review
checklist.tip: Set a recurring Monday calendar event: '15-min activation funnel review'. Consistency beats intensity in activation optimization.

checklist.task: Configure day-2 re-engagement in-app message for demo data users
checklist.tip: Trigger condition: user has activated demo data AND viewed at least 2 distinct reports. Timing: 36–48 hours after demo activation, not 24h — let them settle into the product first.

diagnosis.signal: 61% of signups complete onboarding steps 1 and 2. Only 18% complete step 3 (analytics integration). Of users who skip step 3, 92% churn within 30 days. The activation bottleneck is precise, localized, and structurally solvable without any pricing or product changes.

friction.rootCause: Step 3 requires 6 sequential actions across two platforms before the user has experienced any product value. The cognitive cost of the integration exceeds the user's motivation level at the point in the journey where trust has not yet been established. Value must precede friction.

decisions.label: Add demo data bypass at the integration step
decisions.action: Add a secondary CTA below the integration form: 'Explore with benchmark data →'. This routes users into a fully functional demo environment seeded with anonymized industry benchmark data. Deploy the day-2 re-engagement trigger to convert demo users to real integrations.
decisions.reasoning: Removes the hard gate without eliminating the integration option. Users who experience the aha-moment first return to complete integration within 48 hours at 3–4x the rate of users who were forced to integrate cold. Engineering estimate: 3–5 days.
decisions.tradeoff: Requires building a seeded demo state. Data quality and realism matter — generic placeholder data reduces the aha-moment impact. Invest in realistic industry benchmarks.

decisions.label: Remove the integration gate from onboarding — defer to day 3
decisions.action: Eliminate step 3 from the onboarding sequence entirely. Grant immediate dashboard access with demo data on sign-up. Trigger the integration prompt on day 3 via in-app message after users have viewed 2+ insights. Make integration feel like upgrading, not a prerequisite.
decisions.reasoning: Value precedes commitment. Users who see 2+ real insights in demo mode are 4.1x more likely to complete the integration than users asked to integrate before experiencing any value. This directly inverts the trust equation.
decisions.tradeoff: The dashboard must function meaningfully with demo data alone. If your core value proposition requires live data to be non-trivially better than the demo, this approach requires a high-quality demo layer — not a placeholder.

decisions.label: Replace API key entry with one-click OAuth for the top 3 platforms
decisions.action: Replace the API key form with OAuth buttons for Google Analytics 4, Mixpanel, and PostHog — the platforms 80% of your users are already on. Auto-detect the most common configuration. Reduce the 6-action context switch to a single authorized click.
decisions.reasoning: OAuth eliminates the credential-hunting friction entirely. It is a trusted, recognized pattern. Average integration completion rate for OAuth versus API key: +340%. Prioritize the platform your top 3 user cohorts use most.
decisions.tradeoff: OAuth implementation requires engineering work per platform. Start with the single highest-frequency platform. One OAuth option that covers 60% of users is better than four partially-built integrations.
